pageProps.title: Twelve Footsteps
pageProps.review: Brain scientist Jeong Jae-seung's Twelve Footsteps is an excellent popular science book that looks into the human heart through brain science, views society and the future through complex systems science, and poses new questions to the familiar world.
pageProps.description: Twelve lectures that lead you to an adventure of thought, a forest of intelligence, and a world off the map.
pageProps.content:
## Review If you like ```brain science```, this is a special lecture you must never miss. Recently, my interest shifted from psychology to brain science. I thought that to understand human psychology more deeply, I should know about the more fundamental ```brain```. Perhaps that's why I could read this book more enjoyably and interestingly.
This book makes the reader ask 'why?' about things they took for granted and look at the familiar world and phenomena from a new perspective. I think it is an excellent popular science book that allows one to look into the human heart with the microscope of brain science and view society and the future with the telescope of complex systems science.
